newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Strauss to act on Elite within 30 days.
newsitem.headline: Strauss to act on Elite within 30 days.

text.p: The head of the Strauss family said on Monday they would decide within a month whether to exercise an option to buy out their partner's stake in Elite Industries, one of Israel's leading food manufacturers.

Elite's biggest shareholder, the Federman group, put in motion last Thursday a "Buy Me, Buy You" agreement it has with the Strauss family-controlled Gideon Holdings, which has the second largest stake in Elite, to buy out Gideon.
The terms of the pact between the two feuding partners require Gideon to accept the offer or to buy out the Federmans within 60 days at a 2.5 percent discount to the offer price.
Michael Strauss, chairman of closely held Strauss Dairies, said his family would not need the full 60 days.
"It will take us about a month to decide," Strauss told Reuters.
Federman has offered to pay Gideon Holdings 38 shekels ($11.28) for every Elite 1 ordinary share it has and 67.25 shekels for every par 5 ordinary share for a total of $66 million.
The Federman group has a 13 percent equity holding, which gives its voting rights equal to 26.28 percent.
The Strauss family, which owns Strauss Dairies, holds at least 17.5 percent of equity and 19.1 percent of voting rights in Elite.
Strauss said his family and the Federman group had been at loggerheads over running Elite.

"We saw they had other ideas. Their philosophy and ours didn't match," Strauss said, without giving details. "We thought the ship in stormy weather should have one captain and not two. We told him, 'Mr Federman, with all respect and friendship, it isn't working out'."

Asked about newspaper reports the Strauss family might purchase the Federman stake in partnership with Danone and Unilever, both shareholders in Strauss businesses, he said: "We can do it with our own resources."

But the Federmans have sought outside help. A spokesman for Israeli beverage maker Jaf-Ora Ltd said on Sunday that if Strauss agreed to sell the Elite holding, Jaf-Ora would buy it under an agreement with the Federman family.

The spokesman said Jaf-Ora would be compensated for the costs of making the offer should Strauss buy out the Federmans instead. Newspapers said Jaf-Ora envisaged eventually also buying the Federmans' holding in Elite.
The spokesman said Jaf-Ora would pay approximately $58 million for the holding, valuing Elite at more than $330 million against its Tel Aviv stock market valuation of $244 million as of Thursday.
Elite has undergone far-reaching changes since the Strauss family came on the scene. Much of the company's loss-making European businesses, acquired in 1992, have been closed or sold off.
